meta.notes: A plan that includes everybody before asking anybody. Chairs the tenants' association. Told Mae about the deed at tea, and has to go on living in that sentence. She keeps the window afterwards. Late recognition, one scene only. Never a password.

threads.source: S03. Sunday visit. Adela speaks; Nadia owes. No later scene explains this one.

threads.topic: You took tea at 6C in June.
threads.source: B04. Her guilt arrives as an org chart.
B15, B22, B24. Her cards are not as good and she knows it.
S15. Intentionally entered. Nothing follows "No." Do not edit in passing.

threads.topic: What happens to the rent now?
threads.source: Lore pass AL-04. Treatment section 3 has the association able to resolve to hold the rent; the Arcade tenants are printed paying into court. A motion only. Adds no mechanic, and does not touch the player's own rent.

threads.topic: Has anyone been asking after the shop?
threads.source: Suspect chain, the four men. She does not know what the drawer held.

threads.topic: Is Miss Voss singing at the Association supper?
threads.source: FICTION, invented for the game; see design/V2_ADELA_SOUND_PICTURE_PLOT_2026-11-01.md. Her plan includes too much; she has begun to ask, after. No knowledge of the night man here.

nq_s1.speaker: ADELA
nq_s1.line: Your account is that stool. The short leg is what you owe me.

nq_s2.line: Then put them under it. Night man, leave it, she's solvent when it wobbles. It's how I know she's paying attention.

choices.label: Is that going to the Derby?

nq_s3.speaker: ADELA
nq_s3.line: What did the plate say to the darkroom? "I'm nothing without you, but leave the door shut."

nq_s5.speaker: ADELA
nq_s5.line: It's got a door in it.

nq_t1.line: The association's correspondence shows I raised the clause with the owner as a courtesy, in the presence of the person who found it, so that the owner could not say she was ambushed. I laid that out in three steps. I would like you to find the step where I ought to have kept my mouth shut, because I have had the plans out since July.

choices.label: You told her what the clause meant.

nq_t1s.line: Don't stand there being tactful. It's a load-bearing silence and I didn't sign for it.

nq_t2.line: Yes. In her own parlour. With the date. Six weeks later I'm reading a schedule on a dead woman's bench with a borrowed glass. Put the wrench down or use it.

nq_t3.line: I know exactly what I could have known. That's the whole of my profession. Don't do that.

nq_w1.line: I do. Her log, her pins, my lettering, which comes out like a fire notice. Saturdays I write down what's in the street, because she did. Three-forty, the man in the grey coat. Again. I've scheduled a talk with him for whenever I stop being afraid of his tailor.

choices.label: "Please send an aviation editor." That's you.

nq_w2.line: Because the Speaker patronised somebody on Monday and nothing happened to him. That was not acceptable in April and it isn't now.

nq_w3.line: It came down for Miss Crosson. Don't compliment it. I know what a card looks like when it's trying.

nq_c1.line: I can't get the card right.

nq_c2.line: You wrote the roof notice like that. In July.

nq_c3.line: I thought she'd done it for you.

choices.label: I lent it to myself. I didn't know.

nq_c5.line: She looks from the capitals to the hand.

choices.label: You still owe me for the March plates.

nq_h1.line: There's a motion to pay the rent to the Municipal Court clerk until somebody shows a title. It has sat on the table since August. It wants a second, a ledger and nobody saying the word strike in front of Mr. Wren. I have the ledger.

nq_h2.line: The chair can't second. So the chair will step out for as long as that takes. I've already paid for one sentence in that parlour. I can pay for this one at the clerk's window, and get a receipt.

nq_l1.line: Her log, so you get my capitals. "Sat. 27 Jul., 3.10. Gentleman asks Mr. Ewald what is left in the bottom drawer. Good hat. No name." He's the third this fortnight. Nobody asks that about a shop unless they know what a shop keeps.

nq_l1s.line: If you came to dust, the pins are in the tin. Mind the card in the corner. I haven't finished being rude to it.

nq_l2.line: Nothing. I looked, after the third one. A clean bottom drawer, and you'd have to know to open it. I don't know what it held. Her register has the deed's plates filed to it, and those aren't anywhere either. I tell every good hat the same. None of them believes me.

nq_p1.line: Yes. Two numbers, the raffle, and I've put her down to photograph the committee. She asked me whether she'd agreed to that. I've started asking people. I do it directly after.
